title: El Hecho de Que: Commenting on a Known Fact

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *el hecho de que* from B2 Unit 6: you start with a fact both people already know, and the comment after it takes the subjunctive. Bogotá is a good place for it: the height, the Sunday street closures and the traffic are facts that everyone knows and that people comment on.

sections.title: Fact first, comment after
rows: El hecho de que la ciudad esté a 2600 metros sorprende a muchos visitantes.
*esté* (subjunctive): the fact is known, the comment follows
El hecho de que cada domingo se cierren las calles permite andar en bicicleta.
*se cierren*: subjunctive after *el hecho de que*
El hecho de que el tráfico sea tan intenso preocupa a muchas personas.
the comment *preocupa* stays singular, like *el hecho*

items.spanish: El hecho de que Bogotá esté en una llanura alta sorprende a muchos visitantes.
items.english: The fact that Bogotá is on a high plain surprises many visitors.

items.spanish: El hecho de que haya una Ciclovía desde 1974 muestra que la idea es antigua.
items.english: The fact that there has been a Ciclovía since 1974 shows that the idea is old.

items.spanish: El hecho de que los autobuses vayan llenos preocupa a algunos usuarios.
items.english: The fact that the buses are full worries some users.

items.spanish: El hecho de que tenga tantas bibliotecas explica el título de Ciudad de la Literatura.
items.english: The fact that it has so many libraries helps to explain the title of City of Literature.

sections.content: Always write *el hecho de que*, with *de*. The comment agrees with *el hecho*, which is singular: *El hecho de que lleguen tarde me molesta*, not *me molestan*. After a past verb use the imperfect subjunctive: *El hecho de que lloviera…*.
